error_note: A Coxiella burnetii IgM titer is Q fever serology and says nothing about Yersinia pestis; an antibody titer is also not evidence of bacteremia, so the bridge phenotype is wrong and the pathogen is lost.
Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces) specific IgG is not total IgG; a low antigen-specific IgG has no pathological meaning and does not show hypogammaglobulinemia.
Anti-basement-membrane IgG is a specific autoantibody, not total immunoglobulin; the occasional immunoglobulin rise in subcorneal pustular dermatosis is an IgA paraprotein, unrelated to this test.
Raised ACTH is a real feature of POR deficiency, but a value 1 hour after glucagon stimulation is expected to rise and needs its own criteria; it is not baseline ACTH.
An 8-hour value after an unspecified (XXX) challenge has no defined low; hypoglycemia is in any case a nonspecific feature (207 diseases) and not a characteristic finding of Antley-Bixler syndrome.
Hypoglycemia is a genuine feature of MADD, but a glucose 5 hours into a lactose tolerance test is read as a rise from baseline for lactase deficiency, not as a hypoglycemia screen.
Short stature is carried by over 1,600 diseases, so a low measured height says almost nothing about this syndrome.
The disease record lists hyperglycemia at excluded (0%) frequency, yet a positive association was emitted; the test is also a 4-hour post-load timepoint rather than a baseline glucose.
Raised lactate is true of the disease, but a 2-hour value after an unspecified (XXX) challenge has no defined high, and lactic acidosis is shared by hundreds of disorders.
A high glucose 90 minutes into an IV glucose tolerance test shows impaired glucose disposal by test-specific criteria; it is not the same as baseline hyperglycemia.

A low anti-asialo-GM1 IgM is the normal state for a neuropathy autoantibody and carries no meaning; bridging through the near-root 'Abnormality of immune system physiology' to Leiner disease has no basis.
CD19 cells/cells is a proportion of lymphocytes, while the bridge phenotype is an increased absolute B cell count; a high fraction can reflect low T cells rather than more B cells.
A low or undetectable boysenberry-specific IgE is normal in anyone not sensitised and is not a measure of total immunoglobulin, so it does not point to X-linked SCID.
A qualitative presence result cannot rule out an abnormal concentration; an undetectable IgD is itself compatible with a decreased level, so at most it argues against an elevated IgD.

VE1 immunohistochemistry is a molecular characterisation test that guides targeted therapy in an already diagnosed melanoma (and is positive in many other tumours and naevi); it does not diagnose cutaneous melanoma.
A low erythrocyte heptacarboxylporphyrin has no pathological reading (it is normally near zero), and the specimen is red cells rather than the circulating (plasma) porphyrin the term names.
The code is a panel with no single normal result, and a negative solid-phase phospholipid antibody panel does not exclude lupus anticoagulant or anti-beta2-glycoprotein I, which the term also covers.
The disease record gives the immunoglobulin phenotype as excluded (0%); in addition a low bovine-gelatin-specific IgE is normal and is not total immunoglobulin.
Autoantibody positivity is recorded as explicitly NOT a feature of idiopathic congenital hypothyroidism, and anti-ribosomal P is a lupus-specific antibody with no thyroid relevance.
This is the monocyte percentage of leukocytes in a body fluid, whereas the phenotype is a decreased absolute monocyte count in blood.

Pure tone audiometry documents the sensorineural hearing loss but is identical across all nonsyndromic deafness loci; the specific disease is diagnosed genetically. The context text also names DFNB72 while the term is DFNB15.

A single-frequency, single-ear threshold is one narrow component standing for the whole audiologic work-up (audiometry, ABR, OAE), and hearing thresholds do not distinguish this locus from any other nonsyndromic hearing loss.

ACTH normally rises after insulin-induced hypoglycemia, so a high value at 1.5 hours is not baseline hypercorticotropinemia; ectopic ACTH secretion is also a very rare (<5%) feature of bronchial endocrine tumours.
A low spotted-fever rickettsia IgG titer simply means no serological evidence of exposure; it is infection serology and has nothing to do with metabolism or homeostasis.
Beta-hydroxybutyrate is a ketone body, not a protein; the correct axis is abnormal circulating ketone body concentration (ketosis).
A 15-minute value in an insulin tolerance test precedes the expected ACTH peak, and a blunted stimulated response needs its own criteria; it is not the same as a decreased basal ACTH.

The BDI-II is a self-report severity and screening scale; major depressive disorder is diagnosed by clinical interview against DSM/ICD criteria, as the context's own 'severity grading' wording concedes.
The CDR stages dementia severity of any cause and is used here as a trial outcome; it does not diagnose Lewy body dementia or separate it from Alzheimer disease.

The direction is lost by binding to the nondirectional parent; I believe HPO does have a child term for decreased serum/circulating creatinine (HP:0012101), contrary to the curator note, and it would fit.
The band starts at 1.5 x10^9/L, the hypereosinophilia threshold, which corresponds to HPO's moderately increased eosinophil count; 'severely increased' is defined as above 5 x10^9/L.

190 mg/dL is the lower bound of a risk-enhancer band, not an upper reference limit; non-HDL cholesterol between roughly 130-160 and 189 mg/dL is already raised, so a value below 190 does not rule the phenotype out.

Several bands under NORMAL are the 'neither deplete nor replete' range (12-30 or 15-30 ug/L), which the curator text itself calls indeterminate; those values, and a female-normal 20 ug/L that is low on the male range, cannot rule out a decreased ferritin.
A high total/HDL cholesterol ratio can arise from a high total cholesterol with a normal HDL-C, so the ratio alone does not indicate a decreased HDL-C concentration.
Anti-TPO positivity is found in 10-15% of euthyroid adults and in most Graves disease; it is a risk marker for, not an indicator of, Hashimoto thyroiditis, as the context itself states.

The CTCAE Grade 1 band is given as [1500, open above), which would grade every normal neutrophil count as decreased; Grade 1 is from the lower limit of normal down to 1500/uL. The other bands are sound.
264-916 ng/dL is the harmonized range for healthy non-obese men aged 19-39; the band states no sex, age or unit, and a value in it is grossly abnormal for a woman or a prepubertal child.
